entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner has invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 / Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, seeking quashment of the FIR bearing Crime No. 43 of 2021 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2), 376-D, 506, 114 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
It is not in dispute that the investigating agency has already submitted the charge-sheet before the competent court.
Out of 19 prosecution witnesses cited, 18 witnesses stand examined, and the trial is now at the verge of conclusion.
In the above circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that no useful purpose would be served in undertaking a detailed evaluation of the evidence at this stage.

It is well settled that the power under Section 528 of BNSS/under Section 482 CrPC is to be exercised sparingly, with NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20807 2 MCRC-38357-2025 circumspection, and only in exceptional situations to prevent abuse of the process of law or to secure the ends of justice.
Interference at this juncture would only result in unnecessary delay in the culmination of the trial.

Accordingly, while declining to quash the FIR, this petition stands disposed of with a direction to the learned trial court to make every endeavour to expedite the proceedings and conclude the trial at the Amit Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134317710/
1 earliest, in accordance with law.
